hero.title: Alongside those who decide.
hero.subtitle: I guide people through key decisions and transitions, develop teams, steer disputes towards agreement and set up family governance. Thirty years alongside founders, business owners, senior executives, leaders in their field and families.
hero.credentials: Lawyer, mediator and Executive Guide · formerly Managing Partner and Central Europe Leader, Deloitte Legal · Chair of the Board, Transparency International Czech Republic

intro.title: What my work rests on
intro.body: One deep conviction runs through all my work: no solution — organisational, structural or legal — holds in the long run without working with the people involved, with their mindset, values, relationships and expectations. Behind every situation that calls for a solution there are people and their needs, whether it is an individual, a leadership team, a dispute between partners or a family in generational transition. At the same time, I am still a practising lawyer, and what clients value is exactly this combination: work on relationships and mindset, together with legal realism grounded in long experience.

individual.title: One-to-one
individual.subtitle: For founders, business owners, senior executives and leaders in their field
individual.description: I guide you through key decisions and transitions. I help you name the questions you may already be asking yourself — about your company, your role, your health, your relationships, or where to go from here and what should come next — and reach answers you can stand behind. I know these situations well, both from working alongside others and from having been through many of them myself.

teams.title: Leadership teams
teams.subtitle: For senior leadership and key teams
teams.description: I help develop senior leadership and key teams so that they work as a real team, especially at times when their teamwork will decide more than immediate results. I know how top executive teams function: I have been part of many of them and have led several. So I also know how a team can reach that level.

mediation.title: Mediation
mediation.subtitle: For co-owners, business partners and families in dispute
mediation.description: I steer disputes towards agreement where going to court is not the right path: it is costly, it is not discreet, it usually ends with one side losing, and the relationship between the parties rarely survives it. As a mediator, I know that agreement does not ultimately depend on the law, but on the ability to find, together with the parties, what they still agree on despite the dispute. That is the ground on which we build a solution both sides can accept.

families.title: Family governance
families.subtitle: For families and family businesses
families.description: I work with families on the rules by which they shape their cooperation and make decisions about the business and their assets. I prepare the transition between generations so that it holds the family together rather than pulling it apart. The way there runs not primarily through legal structures, but through the family's values. I know trusts, foundations and holding structures, Czech and foreign, from many years of practice — but the starting point is always work with the family itself.

about.title: About me
about.body: I draw on thirty years of legal practice at PwC, Ambruz & Dark and Deloitte Legal. I co-founded the law firm Ambruz & Dark, and at Deloitte Legal I served as Managing Partner for the Czech Republic, then as Central Europe Leader and a member of the global leadership team. Today, alongside my role as Executive Guide and my own law practice, I serve on the Board of Directors of the Czech Bar Association, where I also lead the Mediation Section, and I have long chaired the Board of Transparency International Czech Republic. I am a certified coach for individuals and teams (QED GROUP) and a mediator (Conflict Management International), and I have trained in crisis intervention (Remedium) and completed the Train to Introduce Mindfulness Course (Oxford Mindfulness Foundation).

contact.title: Let's talk
contact.body: I work with a limited number of clients, so that I can give each of them the attention their situation deserves, over the long term and in confidence. We start with a no-obligation conversation — no expectations, no pitch. Just you and me, to find out whether we want to work together. I work in Czech and English.

hero.title: The higher you rise, the fewer people you can talk to openly about everything — your concerns, your dilemmas, your plans.
hero.subtitle: A long-term working relationship for people whose decisions tend to have far-reaching consequences and who often bear those consequences alone.

sections.heading: Someone to talk it all through with before you decide
paragraphs: I work with people who are dealing with or deciding something fundamental, going through something, or wanting to move forward. I help them name what is really at stake, what matters, and which way forward they will be able to stand behind. I am not a theorist — over the years I have been in similar situations many times, both alongside clients and in my own life.

sections.heading: When it makes sense
items: You are facing a major decision with consequences for your career, your family and beyond
You want to move forward, professionally or personally, and need help both with defining the next goal and with reaching it
You are considering a change but do not know how to get there, or you fear it as a step into the unknown
You are starting a new chapter — a change of role, of company or of what you want from life
The line between work and private life is blurring, and it is starting to hurt
You are looking for new motivation in your career
Your career now takes more than it gives, or is not heading where you want it to, and you do not know where to go next
You notice signs of burnout, dissatisfaction or restlessness, even though from the outside everything seems to work and you tell yourself you ought to be happy

sections.nav: When mediation is better than court
sections.heading: When mediation is better than court
items: Litigation is costly and draining — financially and mentally
Court proceedings are not discreet — hearings are usually public
Litigation almost always damages relationships you want to keep afterwards
Court proceedings usually take years, while an agreement can be reached within weeks
Mediation makes sense even when the case is already in court

sections.heading: Approach
paragraphs: Mediation is a structured process, not an informal meeting. I first help each party put into words how they see the dispute. Together we look for what they agree on despite the conflict and what their real, shared interest is, and on that basis we work towards a solution both sides can live with.

sections.heading: How mediation works
steps: Initial conversations with the parties, separately and together, to clarify what the dispute is about and whether mediation is suitable.
Joint sessions in which we look for what the parties agree on and build a solution on it.
A written agreement. If the parties wish, it can be made enforceable.

sections.heading: Impartiality and confidentiality
paragraphs: In any dispute I mediate, I never act as a lawyer for either party, whether before or after the mediation.
If you have a lawyer, they remain your lawyer. They can accompany you to the mediation and go through the agreement with you before you sign.

As a lawyer, I am bound by professional confidentiality in my role as mediator too. On top of that, we set out the confidentiality of everything said in the mediation in a written mediation agreement, so that it binds both parties as well.

sections.heading: What mediation is not
paragraphs: Mediation is not a softer form of litigation, and I am not an arbitrator. I do not decide who is right and I do not hand down a judgment. My role is to run the process so that the parties reach agreement themselves — and both genuinely want to keep it. I am responsible for the process leading to the agreement; the parties are responsible for its content.

hero.title: Legal rules and tax structures do not hold a family, its assets or its businesses together. Shared values, a common goal and open communication do.
hero.subtitle: I help families define their shared values and how they work together, and then the rules by which they decide together about the family's future, the business and their assets — their family governance. I prepare transitions between generations so that they hold the family together rather than pulling it apart.

sections.heading: Who it is for
items: Founders who are starting to think about who will one day take over the business, and how
Founders who want to protect future generations from pitfalls and risks from outside — and from themselves
Business-owning families looking for more than legal and tax structures for the future of the family and its assets
Family businesses weighing different options and ways of continuing or handing over ownership and management
Established multi-generational structures with several family branches, looking for a way to keep working together in the long term for the benefit of the whole family

sections.heading: When it makes sense
items: Handing over the business is not yet discussed openly in the family, even though everyone knows it will come
The next generation is joining the business, and roles and rules are not clear
Family members have different ideas about what to do with the business and the assets
A structure already exists (a trust, foundation or holding company), but the family does not agree on its purpose

sections.heading: What it covers
items: Family constitution — the family's agreement on values, roles and rules in relation to the family, the business and the assets.
Family council and other bodies where needed — a place and a rhythm for the family to make decisions together and resolve disagreements before they turn into disputes.
Family office — managing the family's assets under one roof; I help decide whether the family needs one and in what form.

Generational transition — planning and aligning expectations about handing over ownership and leadership, their realistic timing and impact, so that both founders and successors are prepared and the rest of the family accepts it.

Planning risk diversification and asset allocation — assets held outside the family for designated beneficiaries, assets structured through succession-law instruments, allocation across different countries and so on.
Fiduciary structures — trusts and foundations, Czech and foreign, including Liechtenstein structures.

sections.heading: Approach
paragraphs: I start with the family, not the structure. Legal and financial arrangements only make sense once they reflect what the family genuinely agrees on — values, roles and expectations. Without that agreement, even the best-written family constitution is just paper.

At the same time, I know the technical side from practice: trusts, foundations including those in Liechtenstein, tax implications and holding structures. So I know what is possible in practice — but the basis is always work with the family and its shared values and expectations.
I work with your lawyers and tax advisers rather than replacing them. If a legal solution is needed, I can prepare it myself or together with your advisers, or they can prepare it themselves.
sections.note: I am Vice-Chair of the Trust and Endowment Fund Administration Subsection of the Czech Bar Association.

sections.heading: How it works
steps: Verifying the brief and refining or adjusting it with the person who commissions the work, typically the founder or head of the family
Discussing the client's ideas about the desired solutions and the ideal final arrangement
Conversations with the relevant family members individually, so that each has room to say how they see the situation and to name any critical points and challenges.

A joint meeting where we name what the family agrees on, where its expectations differ and what needs work, and set out the framework for further cooperation and the steps towards the final arrangement.
Joint meetings to define shared values and related questions, leading to the family constitution.
Only then further documents and structures: the family council, legal arrangements and so on.
Any further legal and related steps towards the final arrangement — ongoing support (where legal services are needed, I provide them separately as a lawyer).
Further support in checking that the arrangement works, and updating documents as circumstances develop.

hero.title: Relationships, mindset and legal realism.
hero.subtitle: This is the combination clients value most in my work. Below is what it means in practice.

sections.heading: Relationships
paragraphs: In most situations people bring to me, what ultimately decides the outcome is not the contract or the strategy, but how the people involved talk to each other. That is what I work with — with one person, a whole leadership team, a family or the parties to a dispute. Besides decades of varied experience, I am trained in individual and team coaching (QED GROUP) and in mediation (Conflict Management International).

sections.heading: Mindset
paragraphs: Pressure, fatigue, doubt, a lost sense of meaning or the first signs of burnout are rarely discussed at the top of companies, even though they affect how a business works far more than we care to admit. I know how to work with this side of things too, again drawing both on my experience of leading teams and on what I have been through myself. I am trained in crisis intervention (Remedium) and in mindfulness (Oxford Mindfulness Foundation).

box.text: I am not a therapist or a doctor. If your situation needs professional care, I will tell you straight away and openly, and help you find the right person. If you are in acute distress, call the Czech crisis line Linka první psychické pomoci on 116 123 (free, 24/7); in a life-threatening emergency, call 155 or 112.

sections.heading: Legal realism
paragraphs: I have been a member of the Czech Bar since 2002, and for many years I led large law firms. I know what is possible legally and in terms of tax, and what is not, and I will not let you base a decision on something that would not hold up. I provide legal services through my law practice; one-to-one guidance, work with teams and families, and mediation are not legal services. When a legal solution is needed, I will tell you, and we will agree on who is best placed to prepare it.

sections.heading: Principles
items: Discretion. Uncompromising confidentiality — I will explain in person the options for securing it.
Impartiality. I have no personal interest in what you decide.
A limited number of clients. I take on only as many engagements as I can give my full attention to.
Where and how. In Czech and English. Ideally at my office in Malá Strana, Prague, otherwise at yours or online.
No price list. We agree on scope and fees after the first conversation, based on what your situation needs.

sections.heading: Why Executive Guide
paragraphs: I chose the word 'guide' deliberately. I do not decide for you, and I do not hand out ready-made answers. I help you see and fully grasp the whole situation, from every angle and with all the options for resolving it. Then I walk with you all the way to a decision that you can stand behind and that will work in the long run.

hero.title: Thirty years in law and leadership. Today, my work is above all about people and relationships.
hero.subtitle: A varied career that makes sense as a whole. Lawyer, mediator and guide for those who make the decisions.

why.heading: How it all fits together
paragraphs: Anyone looking at everything I do today might be tempted, a little ironically, to call me a jack of all trades. I guide people through important decisions and towards their goals, work with teams, mediate disputes, and help families function across generations and pass on family wealth. It took me a while to convince myself that it all makes sense as a whole and that I do not want to give up any part of it.

What connects it all is that each time I am helping people who are facing something fundamental — whether it concerns their company, their family, a team, a dispute or their own mental wellbeing — and who need someone to talk it through with and to stay by their side on the way to a decision. I have met a great many such people over the years. And more than once, I have been in their position myself, with the same questions.

You never deal with anything in isolation from the people around you — colleagues, business partners, friends, family or the other side. And you will always perceive all of reality through a single receiver: your own head and your own mind.
